dehydrated_text:
The problem is that there are people who do real evil in this world. It's possible, like a man kills your daughter, and then he's put in prison for the longest time. Can he be forgiven? The answer is yes, because the only way for this world to work is if people are allowed to be forgiven. If we don't allow forgiveness, this entire universe breaks down. That's why God is a God of forgiveness.

We live in a world of vengeance, right? If you kill my daughter, then I have to go kill your daughter, and then you're going to have to go kill my family, and I have to go kill your family. The only way for this world to work is if we are allowed to forgive each other. Previously, we didn't have a tool to forgive because we ourselves didn't have the wisdom. Now with the arrival of Jesus, we remember that if Jesus forgives us, He will forgive me always. So, if I turn towards Jesus, then I will be forgiven.

But currently, I think I still cannot forgive myself for making that mistake. Like, whatever things I do to make up for the mistake, I think I couldn't forgive myself at that time. But you went to prison, right? You've been punished already. So justice hasn't served its purpose yet. You can now forgive yourself because you've done your time and remember that Jesus forgives you. The only way for you to move on in your life is if you're able to forgive yourself.

If in a world there's no forgiveness, this world would break down really quickly because everyone would just kill each other. Again, what Dante teaches us is that when you grow older and your heart matures with more life experience, you'll understand the importance of forgiveness. At your age, if someone told me this, I'd be like, "You're crazy." This makes no sense because if you do evil, then you should be an evil person for your entire life. If you do evil, evil should come to you.

But what Jesus is saying is that in a world where there's no forgiveness, no one can be happy. The people whose evil has been done to them are so focused on vengeance and hatred that you can never be a happy person. You leave the divine. When you hate someone, you're actually hitting yourself instead of the person.

Now we understand this idea, and now Don is going to explain why we are here. What's the purpose of the universe? Alan says, "I see water, fire, air, and earth, and all they compose harm to corruption and endure so briefly. If what has been said above is true, then these things never should be subject to corruption." God is perfect, everything He creates is perfect. So if that's the case, why do we die? Peter says, "God is perfect; He creates perfection. But He creates the laws of the universe, He creates the game. The things within the game enter a cycle of destruction and life because that's the only way for the game to work properly."
